facts.text: Camrose Colony sits at 48°18′42″N, 111°36′43″W, placing it in southern Toole County, Montana.
Founded in 2001 as a daughter colony of East End Hutterite Colony near Havre, Camrose Colony reflects the Lehrerleut tradition of common ownership.
The colony’s pacifist stance, rooted in Anabaptist non‑resistance, means its members reject military service and political involvement.
Despite limiting TV and radio, Camrose Colony uses GPS‑guided tractors and computers to run its efficient farming operations.
Camrose Colony’s cattle ranching and aquaculture support traditional Hutterite practices while participating in Montana’s Block Management Area #210 for public hunting.
Harsh winters and moderate summers in Camrose Colony shape local environmental dynamics and dictate its agricultural cycles.
